A 50-year-old man with known neurofibromatosis type 1 and multiple cutaneous neurofibromas, and no history of smoking, was admitted for recurrent urinary retention and sepsis. A transurethral resection of the prostate revealed fibroleiomyomatous hyperplasia, but urinary function did not improve. Laboratory studies and a CT scan showed diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall without a discrete mass. Because of compromised bladder function, the patient underwent cystoprostatectomy. 

On gross examination, the bladder wall was diffusely thickened, firm, and gray–white, with near–complete loss of the detrusor muscle. Histologic evaluation revealed in the superficial wall a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix. In the deeper wall, there was a dense, perivascular spindle cell proliferation with prominent cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern. The tumor was in close contact with peripheral nerves. 

Immunohistochemical studies showed that the tumor cells were positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56, and negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin.
